reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster, primarily because it incorporates a dedicated tempo workout and a more structured approach to building threshold strength. Plan B, while including longer runs, focuses heavily on easy runs and general strength work, lacking the specific intensity needed to improve speed. Plan A’s inclusion of a 47-minute tempo session directly addresses the need to increase lactate threshold, a key determinant of running speed. Furthermore, the shorter, more frequent easy runs in Plan A allow for better recovery and adaptation between harder sessions, crucial for a faster runner.
